title: When the Bridge Turns
premise: In the river city of Vellamare, on the eve of the printers' rising, Vesper Almeida has survived three years of occupation by making herself unremarkable in her father's print shop. When a sealed letter hidden in a case of type names the Almeidas as conspirators in an assassination plot they never joined, Vesper realizes the letter is bait: whoever controls it will decide who hangs when the revolution comes. Over one desperate night she must gather testimony from witnesses who would rather stay silent, set the true account in type, and print it before the victors' historians can sail away with the official story at morning tide. She succeeds at terrible cost—her father is arrested in her place, and Vesper chooses to stay in the burning city, becoming the keeper of the record rather than the invisible daughter she once was.
about_author: Oscar Dunmore is the pen name of a former typesetter's apprentice who spent a decade restoring letterpress equipment in coastal archives before turning to fiction. He writes about ordinary people caught between history's machinery and its ink.

chapters.title: The Weight of Quiet Type
chapters.summary: Vesper Almeida, POV. Establishes daily life in the Almeida print shop under occupation: which customers to serve slowly, which soldiers to ignore, which silences keep people safe. Vesper demonstrates her skill reading people and type alike. Emotional beat: wary competence masking exhaustion; the reader feels how much invisibility costs.

chapters.title: A Letter in the Case
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Sorting confiscated type returned by the garrison, Vesper finds a sealed letter wedged behind the em quads, naming her family among plotters against the Governor. Her father burns to destroy it; Vesper notices the seal is wrong—the wax is a forgery. Emotional beat: dread curdling into suspicion that someone wants them framed.

chapters.title: What the Compositor Saw
chapters.summary: Alternating Vesper and her father Tomas. They trace the forged seal to a journeyman compositor, Rell, who vanished after setting work for the Governor's secretary. Tomas forbids inquiry; Vesper visits Rell's widow, who reveals he was paid to plant the letter—and that he drowned before he could spend the money. Emotional beat: grief opening a door to defiance.

chapters.title: The Historians' Ship
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. She learns a chartered vessel, the Meridian, will sail on the morning tide carrying the regime's sanctioned account of the coming uprising—written to blame the print shops. The scale of the lie becomes clear: not just her family, but the whole quarter. Emotional beat: private fear expanding into righteous anger.

chapters.title: Witnesses Who Would Rather Forget
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV, with interludes from dockworker Sefa. Vesper begins collecting sworn statements: the harbormaster's clerk, a defected soldier, Sefa herself. Each witness demands something—money, silence, protection. One betrays her meeting to the garrison. Emotional beat: the grinding, imperfect labor of building truth outside any court.

chapters.title: Setting the Record
chapters.summary: Tomas and Vesper, alternating. Working by candlelight, they compose the true account in secret, page by page, while the city outside grows restless and the first barricades go up. Tomas confesses he once printed for the old tyrant too—a reckoning with his own complicity. Emotional beat: father and daughter reconciled through shared craft and shared guilt.

chapters.title: The Raid on Quay Street
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Soldiers storm the shop hunting the letter and the press. Tomas sends Vesper out the coal chute with the locked forme of type and stays behind; he is arrested as the presses are smashed. From a rooftop Vesper watches everything she knew burn. Emotional beat: devastating loss transmuted into resolve—she now carries the record alone.

chapters.title: Borrowed Presses
chapters.summary: Sefa and Vesper, alternating. Vesper turns to the underground: a smugglers' press aboard a moored barge, run by people the regime never counted. Bargaining, threats, and Sefa's hard-won loyalty get her a night of press time—but only if the tide serves and the garrison stays distracted by the rising. Emotional beat: belonging found among the overlooked.

chapters.title: When the Bridge Turns
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Climax. As the uprising peaks, the drawbridge—the city's throat—turns against the crowd, raised on the secretary's order to trap them. Vesper must choose: use the last hour of darkness to print, or help Sefa force the bridge down and save lives. She does both, printing with powder smoke in her lungs as the bridge groans open. Emotional beat: justice and mercy refusing to be separated.

chapters.title: Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Vesper, POV. Dawn. The Meridian prepares to sail with the victors' false history; Vesper's broadsheet, wet off the smugglers' press, is already in a thousand hands along the quay, read aloud over the crowd. Tomas is freed from a holding pen by the very witnesses he once feared. Vesper declines passage offered by fleeing officials' clerks and stays, founding the city's free press. Emotional beat: quiet triumph—belonging earned, power answered with the record.
